content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"CORE_ONLY","rationale":"The book's core identification — that the biblical Name of God functions as the covenant identity of a house, whose substance is the three ark items the Head provides (Word/manna, covenant law/tables, appointed fruitful priesthood/rod) — is carried by an unusually tight textual chain: the ark itself is 'called by the name of the LORD' (2 Sam 6:2); God converts David's request for an ark-house into 'an house for my name' (2 Sam 7:13); Solomon explicitly equates building the house for the Name with setting there the ark 'wherein is the covenant' (1 Kgs 8:20-21); Hebrews 9:4 inventories exactly three contents; and Deut 8:3, Deut 4:13, and Num 17:5,8 each supply Scripture's own definition of one item. The strongest counter — the mainstream reading that 'name' means the revealed character, presence, reputation, and authority of the person (including Deuteronomistic 'name-dwelling' presence theology) — is broader, not contradictory: covenant identity of a house is a specification of whose identity and how it is constituted, and the common view itself lists 'covenant ownership/belonging' and 'name dwelling in the sanctuary' as facets. The counter cannot explain why the house 'for my name' is functionally the house for the ark, why the ark bears the Name, or why its three contents are each independently defined by Moses as word, covenant, and chosen priesthood; it must treat those convergences as coincidence. The counter also handles Isa 4:1 (women wanting the man's name without his bread or garment) less specifically than the book, which reads it as claiming household identity while refusing the Head's provision — matching Matt 7:22-23 and Deut 28:58's binding of the Name to obedience. No supplied text is inexplicable under the book's core. However, the secondary elaborations — the exact redefinition of 'taking the name in vain' as rejecting any one pillar, and the counterfeit-Name taxonomy — extend beyond what the cited texts compel, so support is limited to the core.","book_core_identification":"A Name is the covenant identity of a house, constituted by three things appointed and provided by its Head: the Word (manna), the covenant law (stone tables), and the fruitful, divinely appointed priesthood (Aaron's budded rod) — demonstrated by the identity between the 'house for my name' and the house built to contain the ark that carries these three items.","book_secondary_elaborations":["A counterfeit Name substitutes a different word, covenant, or priesthood under another head (Babel, the beast's name)","The Name is 'taken in vain' specifically when any one of the three pillars is rejected, replaced, or removed","A bride takes her Husband's Name by entering His house, coming under His authority, and obeying Him (Isa 4:1; Eph 5; Ezek 16)","Prayer 'in Jesus' Name' means asking as a member of His house in agreement with His revealed will, not attaching a formula","The Lord's Prayer maps petition-by-petition onto the ark's contents (daily bread = manna/Word; forgiveness of debts = covenant law; deliverance = priestly intercession)"],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The mainstream reading combined with Deuteronomistic name theology: 'name' symbolizes the revealed character, identity, reputation, authority, and manifest presence of the person who bears it; God's causing His 'name to dwell' in the temple is a mode of divine presence and invocation (2 Sam 6:2 'dwelleth between the cherubims'; 1 Kgs 8:27-29), the ark's contents are historical covenant memorials with no definitional relation to the Name, Ex 20:7 forbids false or empty invocation of God, and Isa 4:1 simply shows that bearing someone's name signifies belonging.","counter_core_identification":"The Name is the person himself as revealed — his character, presence, reputation, and authority — not a structured covenant constitution; texts about the name dwelling in the house concern God's presence and invocation, and the ark's
